name: Jakarta
operatingHours: MRT Jakarta (North–South line, Lebak Bulus–Bundaran HI) runs ~5:00 AM–midnight, every ~5 min at peaks and ~10 min off-peak; the extension north to Kota is still under construction. LRT Jabodebek runs ~5:00 AM–~11:00 PM and LRT Jakarta (Kelapa Gading–Velodrome) ~5:30 AM–~11:00 PM. KRL Commuter Line trains run ~4:00 AM–midnight. TransJakarta BRT covers the gaps, with some corridors running 24 hours.
fareInfo: Pay with a contactless bank e-money card (Flazz, Brizzi, e-Money, TapCash) or the JakLingko app; single-trip QR tickets also work on MRT. MRT Rp4,000–14,000 by distance; LRT Jakarta flat Rp5,000; LRT Jabodebek Rp5,000 + Rp700/km, capped at Rp10,000 off-peak / Rp20,000 peak; KRL Rp3,000 for the first 25 km + Rp1,000 per extra 10 km; TransJakarta flat Rp3,500 (Rp2,000 before 7:00 AM). Fares as of Jan 2026.

sights.name: Jakarta Aquarium & Safari
sights.note: A large indoor aquarium in the Neo Soho mall at West Jakarta, mixing marine tanks and walk-through tunnels with small animal exhibits and feeding shows.

sights.name: Istiqlal Mosque
sights.note: Southeast Asia's largest mosque, a vast modernist hall for over 100,000 worshippers facing the Catholic cathedral; free guided tours for visitors outside prayer times.
sights.hours: Visitor tours ~8:00 AM–5:00 PM outside prayer times; modest dress required

sights.name: Kota Tua (Fatahillah Square)
sights.note: The cobbled square at the heart of old Dutch Batavia, ringed by colonial buildings turned museums, with rental bikes and the historic Café Batavia.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; museums ~9:00 AM–3:00 PM, closed Mon

sights.name: National Monument (Monas)
sights.note: A 132 m obelisk topped by a gilded flame in the middle of Merdeka Square, with a history diorama hall underground and a lift to the top deck.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun ~8:00 AM–4:00 PM plus evening session ~7:00–10:00 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: National Museum of Indonesia
sights.note: The country's main museum, known for its elephant statue, with Hindu-Buddhist stone sculpture, ethnographic collections and gold treasures; reopened in 2024 after a fire.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–4:00 PM, Tue–Sun (later on some weekends); closed Mon

sights.name: Taman Mini Indonesia Indah
sights.note: A sprawling culture park in East Jakarta with traditional houses from every province, museums and a cable car over a lake shaped like the archipelago.
sights.hours: ~7:00 AM–10:00 PM daily (pavilions and museums shorter)

sights.name: Ancol Dreamland
sights.note: A seafront leisure district on Jakarta Bay with beaches, the Dufan amusement park, Sea World and Ocean Dream; each attraction is ticketed separately.
sights.hours: Gates open 24 hours; Dufan ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Jakarta Cathedral
sights.note: A neo-Gothic Catholic church from 1901 with spiky steeples and a small museum upstairs, directly across from Istiqlal Mosque.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–5:00 PM outside Mass; museum shorter hours

sights.name: Museum Bank Indonesia
sights.note: A well-presented free museum in the former Javasche Bank building, covering Indonesian money and economic history with Art Deco interiors and stained glass.

sights.name: Wayang Museum
sights.note: Shadow puppets, wooden golek puppets and masks from across Indonesia and beyond, in a colonial building on Fatahillah Square.

sights.name: Glodok Chinatown
sights.note: Jakarta's Chinatown, where Petak Sembilan's lanes of herbalists and snack stalls lead to the smoky 17th-century Dharma Bhakti temple.
sights.hours: Best in the morning; temples ~6:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Sunda Kelapa Harbour
sights.note: The old port where wooden pinisi schooners still load cargo by hand, near the Maritime Museum and the leaning Syahbandar tower.

sights.name: Jalan Surabaya Flea Market
sights.note: A street of small stalls in leafy Menteng selling vintage vinyl, old cameras, brassware and curios; bargain hard.

sights.name: Ragunan Zoo
sights.note: A large, shady zoo in South Jakarta known for its primate centre and Indonesian species such as Komodo dragons and orangutans; popular with families at weekends.

railStations.name: Gambir
railStations.note: The main station for executive-class intercity trains to Bandung, Yogyakarta, Semarang, Surabaya and Malang, on the east side of Monas; KRL commuter trains do not stop here.
railStations.hours: Intercity trains ~5:00 AM–~10:00 PM by timetable.

railStations.name: Pasar Senen
railStations.note: Hub for economy and business-class trains east across Java, with KRL commuter platforms (Bogor/Cikarang loop) on the subway map.
railStations.hours: Intercity trains by timetable, including overnight; KRL ~4:00 AM–midnight.

railStations.name: Halim
railStations.note: Jakarta terminus of the Whoosh high-speed railway to Bandung (Tegalluar) in ~45 min, linked to Halim LRT Jabodebek station on the subway map.
railStations.hours: Whoosh ~6:00 AM–~9:30 PM; LRT ~5:00 AM–~11:00 PM.

airports.name: Soekarno–Hatta International Airport
airports.transitNote: The airport train (on the subway map) runs from the Skytrain station by Terminals 1–3 to BNI City/Sudirman Baru (for MRT Dukuh Atas) and Manggarai in ~46 min for ~Rp70,000–85,000, every ~30 min; a free Skytrain links the terminals. DAMRI buses and taxis take 45–90 min to the centre depending on traffic.
airports.hours: Airport train from CGK ~5:57 AM–~10:57 PM; from Manggarai ~5:00 AM–~10:00 PM.

airports.name: Halim Perdanakusuma International Airport
airports.transitNote: A smaller airport in East Jakarta used by some domestic flights; no rail link of its own. Taxi or Grab ~10 min to Halim LRT/Whoosh station, ~30–60 min to Thamrin; TransJakarta buses also stop outside.
